function.name: ProductSearch_execute
function.description: Performs a search for products in the database based on specified criteria, such as keywords and filters, and returns a list of matching products. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

keywords.description: The search terms used to find products, separated by spaces.

category.description: The category to filter the search results. If no category is specified, all categories will be included in the search.

price_range.description: A price range to narrow down the search results, specified as a string in the format 'min-max' where min and max are prices in USD.

sort_order.description: The order in which the search results are sorted. Choose 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

in_stock.description: A flag to filter search results to only include products that are in stock. Set to true to include only in-stock items.

message.reasoning: The user says: "Warna pink kapan restok kak". This is Indonesian: "When will the pink color restock?" They want to know when the pink color product will restock. We need to respond appropriately. We can ask clarifying question: which product? Or we can provide general info: we don't have real-time inventory. We can say we can't check real-time but we can search for product with keyword "pink" maybe. But we need to use the function to search for products. The user didn't specify product name. We could ask them to specify product. But we can also search for "pink" in all categories. Let's do a search for "pink" across all categories. Use function ProductSearch_execute with keywords "pink", category unspecified, price_range unspecified, sort_order asc, in_stock true. Then we can get results. But we might not get restock info. The function returns matching products. We can then see if any product has "pink" and maybe show availability. But we cannot get restock date. So we can respond: "We don't have real-time restock info. Let me search for pink products." Then call function.
